learningObjectives.title: The Wall Street Crash and Depression

questions.q: Which 1922 tariff act raised US import duties to protect American industry from foreign competition?
questions.explain: The Fordney-McCumber Tariff of 1922 placed high duties on imports to shield US industries and boost domestic demand.

questions.q: Which industry, transformed by Henry Ford's assembly-line mass production, boomed most in 1920s America?
questions.explain: Ford's assembly line made cars cheap and plentiful, making the motor car industry the leading symbol of 1920s prosperity.

questions.q: The national ban on making and selling alcohol, introduced by the 18th Amendment in 1920, was known as what?
questions.explain: Prohibition banned alcohol from 1920 but led to bootlegging, speakeasies and organised crime.

questions.q: Why did the growth of the motor car industry help many other American industries in the 1920s?
options: It created huge demand for steel, rubber, glass and petrol
It reduced the need for factory workers across the country
It encouraged Americans to save rather than spend
It lowered the tariffs on imported goods
questions.explain: Car production consumed vast quantities of raw materials and fuel, stimulating steel, rubber, glass, oil and road-building industries.

questions.q: Which group did NOT generally share in the prosperity of the 1920s?
questions.explain: Overproduction and falling prices meant farmers struggled with debt and low incomes throughout the decade.

questions.q: What is meant by 'speculation' on the stock market in the 1920s?
options: Buying shares hoping to sell them quickly for a profit
Storing gold reserves in the Federal Reserve
Paying for goods in monthly instalments
Investing savings safely in government bonds
questions.explain: Speculators gambled that rising share prices would let them sell quickly for a profit rather than holding shares long-term.

questions.q: Why did membership of the Ku Klux Klan grow rapidly in parts of the USA during the 1920s?
options: Many white Americans were hostile to Black people, immigrants and Catholics
It offered financial help to unemployed workers
It campaigned peacefully for the end of Prohibition
It supported greater rights for immigrant communities
questions.explain: The revived Klan exploited widespread racism and intolerance towards Black Americans, immigrants, Catholics and Jews.

questions.q: In which month and year did the Wall Street Crash take place?
questions.explain: Share prices collapsed on the New York Stock Exchange in October 1929, triggering the Great Depression.

questions.q: The day of massive panic selling on 29 October 1929 became known as what?
questions.explain: On Black Tuesday, 29 October 1929, around 16 million shares were sold as prices collapsed.

questions.q: What did it mean to buy shares 'on the margin' in the 1920s?
options: Paying only a fraction of the price and borrowing the rest
Buying shares only from government-owned companies
Purchasing shares directly from a factory
Selling shares before their price had risen
questions.explain: Buying on the margin meant borrowing most of the cost of shares, which magnified losses when prices fell.

questions.q: Why did thousands of American banks collapse in the early 1930s?
options: Savers rushed to withdraw money and borrowers could not repay loans
The government seized all their gold reserves
They were banned from lending under Prohibition
Foreign banks bought them out and closed them
questions.explain: Panic withdrawals combined with unpaid loans and worthless shares left banks without funds, forcing them to close.

questions.q: Which Republican president was blamed for failing to end the Depression and was defeated in the 1932 election?
questions.explain: Hoover's belief in limited government action made him deeply unpopular, and he lost the 1932 election to Roosevelt.

questions.q: In the early 1930s over-farming and drought turned large parts of the Great Plains into a region of destructive dust storms. What was this area called?
questions.explain: The Dust Bowl saw topsoil stripped away by dust storms, ruining farms and forcing families to migrate.

questions.q: What did Roosevelt promise the American people in his 1932 election campaign?
questions.explain: Roosevelt promised a 'New Deal' of government action to tackle unemployment and revive the economy.

questions.q: What name was given to Roosevelt's reassuring radio broadcasts to the American people?
questions.explain: In his 'fireside chats' Roosevelt used the radio to explain his policies and restore public confidence.

questions.q: In 1933 a farmer is paid by the government to reduce his cotton acreage and slaughter surplus piglets to push up prices. Which New Deal agency is responsible?
questions.explain: The AAA paid farmers to cut production so that reduced supply would raise farm prices and incomes.

questions.q: An unemployed young man is given work planting trees and building flood defences in national parks for a monthly wage. Which New Deal agency employs him?
questions.explain: The CCC gave unemployed young men paid work on conservation projects such as tree-planting and flood control.

questions.q: Why did Roosevelt set up public works agencies such as the WPA and PWA?
options: To create jobs and reduce unemployment
To ban trade unions from the workplace
To raise tariffs on foreign goods
To close down failing banks permanently
questions.explain: Public works agencies funded schools, roads and dams to provide employment and put money back into the economy.

questions.q: A government scheme builds a series of dams across a river valley spanning several southern states to supply cheap electricity and prevent flooding. Which agency carried this out?
questions.explain: The TVA built dams in the Tennessee valley to control flooding, generate cheap electricity and provide work.

questions.q: Why did the US Supreme Court oppose parts of the New Deal?
options: It ruled some agencies unconstitutional for giving the federal government too much power
It believed the New Deal did not spend enough money
It wanted Prohibition to be reintroduced
It thought too many bankers were being helped
questions.explain: The Supreme Court declared bodies such as the NRA and AAA unconstitutional, arguing they gave the federal government excessive power over states and business.
